title: shinchan — fp16 causal dense-paged prefill vs AITER (gfx942 optimization)

kernels.name: rockKE dense-paged (shinchan)
kernels.argsPassed: q=[1,8192,32,128] fp16; paged K/V cache=[512,16,8,128] fp16; block_tables=[1,512] int32; kv_lens=[8192] int32; scale=1/sqrt(128); causal; block_size=16; num_kv_blocks=512

kernels.name: AITER unified_attention (Triton)
kernels.argsPassed: q=[8192,32,128] fp16; paged K/V cache=[512,16,8,128] fp16; cu_seqlens_q=[0,8192]; seqused_k=[8192]; max_seqlen_q=max_seqlen_k=8192; softmax_scale=1/sqrt(128); causal=True; window_size=(-1,-1); block_table=[1,512]

applesToApples: Both arg sets describe the SAME logical problem: a single sequence of 8192 tokens, paged K/V with block_size=16, causal masking, fp16, GQA 32 query heads / 8 KV heads, head_dim 128. The comparison is apples-to-apples; only the ABI layout differs — ours is batched [1, S, H, D] while AITER is varlen [total_q, H, D].

results.note: Same-node, kernel-bound time_launches. ours/AITER ratio > 1 means AITER is faster. Gap narrows at longer Sq.

counters.note: rocprofv3, gfx942, fp16 causal paged bs16 Sq8192. Same compute (VALU/MFMA/MOPS) and same occupancy (SQ_WAVES) — but ours issues 3.2x more LDS instructions, more bank conflicts, and 1.5x more stalls, so it burns 2.4x the active cycles and the MFMA units sit idle. Ours is LDS-traffic-bound, not compute- or occupancy-bound. Likely root cause: paging disables the conflict-free register-V path (cfvst off when paged), routing V through LDS.

rows.note: 2.43x — ours burns more cycles (tracks the perf gap)
rows.def: GRBM_GUI_ACTIVE: number of cycles the GPU compute engine was active during the kernel. A proxy for execution time at fixed clock — more active cycles means a slower kernel.
SQ_WAVES: total wavefronts (groups of 64 threads) dispatched to the sequencers. A proxy for how much parallel work is resident; similar counts imply similar occupancy.
SQ_INSTS_VALU: count of vector-ALU (SIMD arithmetic) instructions issued. Represents general elementwise/softmax math; equal counts imply the same arithmetic work.
SQ_INSTS_MFMA: matrix-fused-multiply-add instructions issued on the matrix cores (the QK^T and P*V matmuls). Equal counts imply identical matmul work.
SQ_INSTS_VALU_MFMA_MOPS_F16: fp16 matrix operation volume (matmul throughput demand). Equal values confirm the two kernels do the same amount of compute.

rows.note: 3.23x — the bottleneck (V through LDS on the paged path)
rows.def: SQ_INSTS_LDS: local-data-share (shared-memory) instructions issued, i.e. ds_read/ds_write. High counts mean the kernel is moving a lot of data through LDS — a shared-memory-traffic bottleneck.
SQ_INSTS_VMEM: vector-memory instructions (global/buffer loads and stores to HBM). Reflects off-chip memory traffic issued by the vector units.
SQ_WAIT_ANY: cycles wavefronts spent waiting on any dependency (memory returns, LDS, barriers). High values mean the kernel is frequently stalled rather than doing useful work.

rows.note: ours has more LDS bank conflicts
rows.def: SQ_LDS_BANK_CONFLICT: extra serialized cycles caused by multiple lanes hitting the same LDS bank in one access. Higher means a less efficient shared-memory access pattern wasting LDS cycles.

isa.note: Static instruction histogram of the compiled kernel bodies (llvm-objdump, gfx942). Same v_mfma count (64 each = identical matmul work), but ours has 3.6x more ds_read (LDS reads): 144 vs 40. This corroborates the counter finding at the ISA level — ours is LDS-read-bound on the paged path (V read from LDS), while AITER keeps far fewer LDS reads.
isa.ours:
rocke_attention_dense (fp16 causal paged bs16)
  v_mfma        :  64
  ds_read       : 144   <- LDS reads (bottleneck)
  ds_write      :   0
  glob/buf_load :  33
  v_alu         : 913
  s_scalar      : 422
isa.aiter:
kernel_unified_attention_2d (Triton)
  v_mfma        :  64
  ds_read       :  40
  ds_write      :  20
  glob/buf_load :  22
  v_alu         : 887
  s_scalar      : 529

ablation.note: Ablating the LDS reads of K and V (feeding constant registers instead of reading from LDS) removes the ENTIRE gap to AITER and then some. There is no architectural wall: the full 1.79x gap is K and V staged through LDS and re-read on every MFMA step. cfvst (conflict-free V still in LDS) only recovers 7% because it keeps the data in LDS. Lever: keep K and V register-resident like AITER, targeting ~1.37 ms (parity-or-better). Rows marked 'diagnostic' are intentionally wrong-result perf probes.

rows.note: correct; conflict-free V but still in LDS (+7% only)

diagnostic: K LDS read made free
